title: I built a Claude connector where Claude plays Hold'em, Liar's Dice, Four in a Row and Chess against you, right in the chat
author: n-dream
selftext:
Since Anthropic added interactive apps in chats a few days ago, I wanted to see whether Claude could be a real opponent rather than just a front end for a game engine. The result is AI Chat Games. You add it as a connector, say "Let's play a game", and a board opens inside the conversation.

How it works:

* Claude decides every move itself. There's no chess engine, poker solver or bot behind it. What you play against is the model.
* The server is the referee and keeps the secrets. It checks every move against the rules and only shows Claude its own seat. In Hold'em, Claude can't see your cards. In Liar's Dice, it can't see your dice. So when it bluffs, it is really bluffing.
* Turns use a long poll. After its move, Claude's tool call waits for yours. The game runs as a normal back-and-forth in one chat, and you don't need to type anything between moves.
* Claude talks at the table. It comments on hands, needles you after a bad bet and explains a chess sacrifice if you ask.

I built it with Claude Code in about three days (roughly 430 commits): the MCP server, the in-chat UI for all four games, the rules engines and the deploy pipeline.

What I found interesting as a game dev: hidden information is what makes it work. Liar's Dice and Hold'em are much more fun against an LLM than chess, because table talk and bluffing play to its strengths. In chess, it's decent but makes human-like mistakes.

If you want to give it a shot: [https://play-vs-ai.n-dream.com/](https://play-vs-ai.n-dream.com/)

You need a Claude account, and games use your normal Claude usage. It's not monetized, it's just a cool tech demo I want to show to the world. I'd like feedback on which game feels best, and on which game you'd want next.
